concepts.def: Memory built using schemas, not recorded exactly.

walkthroughs.body_html: Bartlett read a Native American folk tale to British participants and asked them to recall it. They shortened, changed and rationalised details to fit British schemas — evidence that memory is reconstructive, not a perfect recording.

The Gestalt school argued 'the whole is greater than the sum of the parts'. Key laws are similarity, proximity, continuity and closure. They explain why we see dotted lines as a circle or rows as columns.

Gibson (direct theory): perception is bottom-up — all needed info is in the optic array. Gregory (constructivist): perception is top-down — we use prior knowledge to make a 'best guess', which is why illusions trick us.
